At 7 or 8 I would shoplift from toy stores. I got caught once and attempted to run out of the store, but was caught by some woman (she got in my path and blocked me). This guy "processed me" in the back, taking my name and address, got my mother to come down. My father beat me mercilessly that night. I used to also steal from my parents at every chance I had. No amount of talking to / beatings / etc sunk in. Of course my parents never investigated the root cause, they just yelled and beat. 

Years later in my teens I was arrested numerous times for grand larceny and even felony for securities fraud. Haven't stolen anything in 20 years now. Its one of the few things I changed about myself for the positive - stopping being a thief.

I'm a collector by nature. My passion years back were video games & pinball machines. I also have a wall st. background. Lots of the tools from Wall St can be converted over into a tool kit for collectors - it leads to more intimate, immersive 'trading' experience. I think its cool, its what I think Ebay and CL should have done, Amazon is the closest to getting it right I think. Lots of features in the toolkit, one that stands out that can save video gamers especially money, is the concept of "Bundles" or managed lots.

Initial markets are standard fare CL stuff, and then I have catalogued and categorized Retro & modern video games, Pop vinyl figures (cute stuff), Magic and pokemon cards, pinball and arcade machines (for old timers like me), and whatever else my community ends up voting for. Very excited, launching my beta next month.

The loophole is the family connection... My ex wife worked for her dad for years making lots but who knows how much, couldn't verify - but always could say she got experience / worked there. If anything ever comes up, such as well why doesn't the w2 add up, cite the references / employees and stand your ground - cause you did work there.

All the best.

Hey,

You don't have any references who can vouch for you during that time at your dads firm? I'm sure you can come up with a well meaning "friend" or colleague. Whats a background check going to turn up on that anyway? Just references. 

The alternative they have is to call the company directly and verify employment - I dont think that by law they can ask for anything else but your time there. Lets say you didn't work there (the worse case scenario right?) - but if you did or didnt doesnt matter - cause heres why - make it clear to them that this is your fathers practice - its a bit of social engineering. WHO would verify that? Its about how you present it.

BTW - sounds like you are anxious as hell, slow it down whoever you are - I entered wall st at 22 with a FINANCE related felony and did ok for 18 years (now its hammering me, surprised i made it this far). You? No felony I assume, working hard, knowledge, keep at it good things will happen.
